description: FHReD, the Future Hydropower Reservoirs and Dams Database, was started within the SMART river science programme to give geographically explicit information on the new hydropower dam boom driven by climate mitigation. The version on the Global Dam Watch page is a beta published with Zarfl and colleagues' 2015 paper, described as for test purposes only; it holds 3,700 records of hydropower dams with a capacity above 1 MW, collected from the peer-reviewed literature, public databases and contributions from non-governmental organisations, and managed by the University of Tübingen. A next version with reservoir size was announced for summer 2019, and the page directs users to the Global Dam Watch directory to obtain the data. Coverage: planned and under-construction dams worldwide, at dam locations. Access: free; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: the beta is uncorrected, ageing since 2015, and plans change or are cancelled. It supports scenarios on future river fragmentation, hydropower expansion and cascading reservoir operation, and complements the GRanD record of existing dams already in the catalogue.
